sections.content: How many people stayed in Norwich after gaining qualifications?

Norwich is a large town in the East of England. Norwich also has a university.

Norwich has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Norwich ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 6,810 state-school pupils from Norwich who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,695 (25%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,890 (28%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Norwich to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Norwich's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Norwich in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Norwich move to?

Of Norwich's graduates, 680 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 120 of those graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Norwich travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Norwich's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 430 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 240 of those qualified non-graduates (56%) were living fairly locally, in the Norwich travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Norwich's GCSE cohort:

  • 480 graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 130 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 68% of graduates and 44% of qualified non-graduates living in Norwich had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 3,070 graduates and 2,555 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Norwich. This is compared with the 1,695 graduates and 1,890 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 32% of the graduates had also lived in Norwich as GCSE pupils, while 68% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Norwich in 2018 to 2019, 55% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 44% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
